Method · Medici dossier, C14 / v5

A reading must show its evidence.

The 1610 proposal relies on a cipher key, distinctions between glyphs and contextual continuations. These sources of information do not have equal evidential force.

The key and its homophones

The comparison uses a key in manuscript Français 3462, Gallica frame 112. It combines several possible signs for a letter, values representing syllables or words, numbers and nulls. Copying the key is not enough: each manuscript shape must still be assigned to the right entry.[3]

Identifiers A1, A2… refer to homophones in plaintext column A, from top to bottom. They distinguish shapes earlier transcriptions grouped under the same “y”, “c” or “m”. A single value is retained per glyph identifier; its value does not change simply to make one occurrence more plausible.

Reading the key in practice

A homophonic key offers several signs for one letter. Here, A1 and A2 are different shapes proposed as A, while D1 and S3 remain distinct despite a rough transcription as “t”. Actual shapes must therefore be compared, not merely typed letters replaced.

The nomenclator adds shortcuts. Proposed entries a, → ce, x, → en, y, → et, 4 → le pape and 41~ → leurs give units of different lengths. “Leurs” is retained in the raw reading; both 41~→leurs occurrences were explicitly selected, without certifying the entire key.

For example, D1–I2–M4–P2–R1–U3–D1–x,–a, proposes D–I–M–P–R–U–D–EN–CE. This is not independent proof: I2 and U3 are now explicit choices by Brice; the U3 merge remains documented. Inspect the images and notes in f17 L2.

Decisions that change the reading

  1. A documented merge. In f17 L2, old segments 16 and 17 (counting from 1) form tu, one glyph proposed as U3. There are therefore 99 old boxes but 98 edited glyphs. No other insertion or deletion is hidden.
  2. Two different t shapes. The simple cross is assigned to D1, the looped t to S3. Giving them one value spoiled “imprudence” and “timidite”.
  3. Three similar shapes kept distinct. The straight d is proposed as P3, the unbarred delta as M4 and the crossed delta as R3. This matters in “trop” and “arogance”.
  4. A comma is not always a word boundary. Entries such as EN and CE can occur inside “imprudence”, “malice” and “arogance”.
  5. Overlining is preserved. An overlined code absent from the applicable key cannot fall back to the simple number. Earlier fallback from 72~ to 72 or 79~ to 79 produced unsupported words for those occurrences.

39~ → le is now explicitly selected. j, → de remains undecidable: “J with a small bar” does not confirm that entry. They are documented in the notes and corresponding cells without replacing the research history.

This summary follows the C00–C10 research journal. No experiment was rerun to build the site. Recorded outcomes retain their historical scope rather than becoming new validation.

Two review protocols with different scopes

Shape comparison with context initially hidden. C11 shows glyph comparisons and lets the reviewer reveal the sentence. Shape choices, free descriptions, code plausibility and observed overlines remain separate. C12 integrates 25 answers; its 12 initial explicit choices are not automatically propagated to other occurrences.

Compatibility test with context. C13 displays the expected character in the proposed word and asks possible, impossible or undecidable. Shape matches and observations stay separate. C14 records 3 possible, 5 undecidable and none impossible. “Possible” fixes no value; “impossible” would exclude the proposed word as written. The B/C conflict is reopened: the earlier B1 choice is retained, with C2 now possible rather than exclusive.

Document transcriptions mark unconfirmed characters in brackets. A reading hypothesis remains distinct from an established value; characters outside this review remain working readings.

Competing strategies

  1. Palaeography and segmentation. Compare the five undecidable points across occurrences before completing a word.
  2. A changed or incomplete nomenclator. Find 72~, 79~, 86~ and 90~ in a complete applicable key, then test another message without adjusting values to its meaning. R2077 is a documentary comparison lead, not a newly executed test here.
  3. Added or changed homophones. Establish whether the two “barred tilde” shapes are identical, and whether their value can be determined independently of “recognoissant” or “sentant”.
  4. Incorrect proposed words. Seek another reading explaining every sign and the grammar without opportunistic corrections. A variant key alone is not a solution.

A fixed homophonic substitution allows several signs for one letter, not two letters for the same sign. If the “barred s” shapes were identical but required S and Z, changing the fixed substitution would not remove the contradiction. Reconsider the shapes, proposed words, plaintext insertion or copying error. A shared description does not establish shape identity. Inspection of frames 108–110 found no exact variant; it does not exclude another key elsewhere.

What the checks establish

The 99 old boxes are still covered exactly once by 98 glyphs, retaining the tu→U3 merge. Boxes and source images have not changed. Assigned identifiers retain one value; unresolved glyphs are not given values to restore expected words.

Reviews integrated — 16 October 2026. Of 98 glyphs: 11 explicit choices retained, 3 possible values, 5 undecidable, 6 plausible but unproved code occurrences, and 73 working readings outside this review. Some characters remain probable but unconfirmed.

Hashes and coverage establish traceability. Human review supplies choices and constraints for certain occurrences, not complete proof of the plaintext or the exact key’s identity. No new solver was run for this update.
